article.body_html:
A reset or stolen phone takes more than contacts with it. If your pickup photos, the contract picture and the payment receipt were all on that one device, the record of what you agreed and what you collected is suddenly thin. That is stressful, but it is a record problem and not a reason to avoid the shop. Rebuild what you can, tell the shop early and calmly, and arrive at the return with an honest account of the bike as it is now.

First, write down what you remember

Before the details fade, put these on paper or in a note on another device:

  • the date and approximate time you collected the bike, and the name of the person you dealt with if you remember it;
  • the bike model and colour, and the plate number if you noted it anywhere;
  • marks you saw on the bike when you took it, and anything the shop pointed out;
  • the fuel level and the odometer reading if you recall either;
  • what you paid, how and when, and what the shop said about the deposit.

Mark anything you are unsure of as unsure. An account that says "I think the left mirror was already scratched" is more useful than one that sounds certain and turns out to be wrong.

Where proof may still exist

Place to lookWhat it may hold
A cloud photo backup or a shared albumPickup photos with their time stamps
Chat history on another device or a web version of the appThe booking message, the quote and any written confirmation
Email and booking confirmationsDates, price and the name of whoever replied
A bank or card statement, or a payment app historyThe date, amount and payee of any card, transfer or app payment (cash leaves no entry, so ask the shop to confirm it in writing)
Your hotel or hostel, if the bike was parked thereA parking note, or a front desk that remembers the bike arriving
A travel companion's phonePhotos taken at the same pickup

Look first, but contact the shop the same day. Walking in with some proof and a clear list of what is missing is easier for everyone than walking in with nothing.

Tell the shop, and ask what it holds

Thuê xe máy Nguyễn Hà is open 09:00–21:00 daily, and its number is 0334 699 969. Call, or use the contact page, as soon as you know the record is gone. A message can be as brief as: "My phone was reset and I lost my pickup photos and receipt for the bike I rented on [date]. Could you tell me what record you hold of the pickup and the payment, and could I see it or have a copy?" Whether the shop keeps its own copy of photos or receipts, and in what form, is for the shop to say. Ask, and write down the answer with the date and the name of the person who gave it.

Do not guess a deposit amount or a payment date to fill a gap. If the shop's version and your memory differ, say so plainly and ask whether the shop has a record and, if so, to be shown it instead of arguing from memory.

If the phone was stolen, not just reset

Secure the accounts before you chase the record. From another device, lock or erase the phone if you can, change the passwords of your email, cloud and chat accounts, and tell your bank if cards or payment apps were on it. A replacement SIM may be needed to receive the codes that unlock a cloud backup, so sort that out early. If keys or papers for the bike went with the phone, tell the shop the same day.

Rebuild the condition record before you return the bike

You cannot recreate the pickup photos, but you can record the bike's condition today and mark honestly what you do not know about before. Photograph every side, the dashboard with the odometer and fuel gauge, the tyres, the mirrors, and any mark you can see, and keep the original files, which store the date and time. Rental Bike Damage Photos: A Hanoi Handover Shot List gives a full list of angles. Then add a short note beside each photo that says, for example, "scratch on the right fairing: I believe it was there at pickup, I cannot show a photo." Showing the shop an honest set of photos and a clear account is better than hoping that nobody looks at the bike.

At the return

  1. Show the shop what you have: photos, your list from memory and the payment evidence you found.
  2. Ask whether the shop has its own record of the bike at pickup and, if so, to compare the bike with it and to see it.
  3. Ask for a receipt or a written note that states when the bike was returned and in what state.
  4. Keep a copy of everything somewhere other than the phone you carry: a cloud folder, an email to yourself or a second device.

Returning a Rental Motorbike in Hanoi: A Receipt and Handover Checklist lists what a receipt should show, and Hanoi Motorbike Rental Deposits: How to Record Payment and Return explains how to keep the payment record so that this situation is less painful next time.
